ai.description: *Micrixalus frigidus* is a small frog (21–24 mm) with a brown dorsum and cream-colored venter. It is distinguished by a white throat and the male’s habit of foot-flagging near cold mountain streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus frigidus* is best distinguished by its unique, vivid yellow-to-orange throat patch, which is absent in most other sympatric dancing frog species.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus frigidus* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found along rocky, shaded streams at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Micrixalus frigidus* is a diurnal frog that performs "foot-flagging," extending and waving its hind legs to communicate with rivals and mates over the noise of rushing water.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus frigidus* is an egg-laying species that breeds during the monsoon. Females deposit small clutches of eggs in hidden nests beneath stream-bed gravel.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus frigidus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting high-elevation streams in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The Cold Stream Dancing Frog emits a high-pitched, rapid series of short, metallic chirps while perched on mossy rocks along fast-flowing, cool mountain streams.
